findings.text: Init-time registration converts a system register descriptor into its architectural encoding and records an index plus one in a forwarding table keyed by encoding, rejecting out-of-range indices and duplicate encodings with an invalid argument failure.
Accessor publishes the GICv3 interrupt controller system register descriptor table together with its element count derived from the table size.

Boot initialization discovers the usable VMID width, warns when the usable ID space does not comfortably exceed the CPU count with ID zero reserved, seeds the allocation generation and allocates a zeroed bitmap; the companion release frees that bitmap.

Guest physical to host mapping helper resolves the memory slot for an intermediate address, validates the host address and writability, performs a capability-selected atomic compare and swap of an eight byte table entry, then marks the page dirty on success.

Each fine-grained trap identity selects a read accumulator and an optional write accumulator for its group; a bit reserved in the read view and also in the write view when present is rejected, otherwise the bit is accumulated into the positive or negative set according to polarity while ignoring reserved positions.

Validation reports any bit claimed by both polarities as invalid, and requires the reserved-clear, reserved-set and both polarity sets to partition the full register width without overlap; on partition failure it logs the inconsistency and recomputes the reserved-clear set as the complement of the other three.

Descriptor ordering is a lexicographic comparison over the five encoding fields in architectural order, with null handling that places a missing entry after any real entry and a fatal check against comparing an entry with itself.

Table audit optionally requires every entry that exposes a user register to provide a reset handler, and always requires strictly increasing encoding order between consecutive entries, failing closed with a diagnostic on the first violation.
Encoding iteration helper walks an inclusive range of thirty-two bit encodings by repeatedly advancing through an architecture-aware successor function.
Early CPU identity capture snapshots the main ID, revision ID and auxiliary ID registers of the boot CPU into dedicated storage for later emulation decisions.

Boot parameter handling maps the none, protected, nvhe and nested requests to internal KVM modes, honoring absence of hypervisor support by ignoring the request, restricting protected mode to non-VHE, and gating the default and nested selections on VHE state, rejecting missing or unknown values.

Wait-for-interrupt and wait-for-event trap controls share a common parser that maps the trap and notrap requests to trap or no-trap states and rejects missing or unknown values, with thin wrappers binding the shared logic to each control.

Address-translation emulation chooses between EL2, EL2 with EL0 access and EL1 plus EL0 regimes from the AT operation kind combined with the virtual E2H and TGE controls when operating from guest EL2.

Effective translation-control extension state is zero for EL1 regime guests lacking nested support for the extension and otherwise reflects the corresponding control register; permission-indirection and overlay enablement additionally require the guest to advertise the respective features, with overlay at EL0 excluded for the pure EL2 regime.

Page-size selection decodes the lower and upper granule fields to four, sixteen or sixty-four kilobyte shifts with architecturally undefined encodings treated as the largest size, checks advertisement in the memory-model register, and falls back to an implemented size preferring the host page size when the programmed size is unavailable.

Output-address validation and extraction account for fifty-two bit physical addressing: size checks use a wider mask when enabled, enablement depends on granule, feature advertisement and physical-size or default state, input address width derives from the size field, and descriptor addresses are assembled with extra high bits for large-address configurations.

Stage-one walk preparation selects control, base and size state according to regime and address range, derives page shift, large-address state, start level and shareability, validates top-bit tagging and sign extension, and takes an MMU-disabled fast path when virtualization controls or the MMU-enable bit disable translation, checking the result against the physical-address limit.

When translation is enabled the walk computes hardware-update, hierarchical-disable, indirection and overlay state, enforces size, granule, range, walk-disable and EL0-disable constraints as translation faults, derives the output-size limit from the physical-size field, aligns and validates the table base, and reports base problems as address-size faults.
Stage-one descriptor accessors honor the guest endianness recorded in the walk state, converting between host order and little or big endian on both plain reads and compare-and-swap updates.

User-accessible atomic descriptor replacement is dispatched by final CPU capability to one of three implementations covering a newer unprivileged sequence, a large-system-extension sequence, or a load-exclusive plus store-exclusive loop, each validating access faults and signaling mismatch for retry.
Descriptor replacement requires the caller to already hold the KVM SRCU read lock, enforced by a lock assertion at entry.
Filter-group accumulator observed to carry separate reserved-clear and reserved-set views, separate positive and negative trap sets, and a descriptive name used in diagnostics.
System-register descriptor observed to carry five encoding components, a name, an optional user register handle and an optional reset handler used by table validation and forwarding setup.

Stage-one walk context observed to carry regime, size and granule state, large-address and output-limit state, shareability, endianness, disable and permission-feature flags, table base, hardware-update state, start level and EL0-access indication, with a separate result carrying fault state, level and physical address.

Walk setup terminates in one of four outcomes: success with a validated base for continued lookup, MMU-disabled success with identity physical address, address-size fault attributed to level zero, or translation fault attributed to the computed start level.
Each atomic replacement reports success, an access fault to propagate, or a mismatch requiring the caller to retry; the exclusive-loop variant also treats a failed store-conditional as a retry.
Boot-time entry points perform one-shot registration and validation of trap masks, system-register forwarding, VMID allocation and mode plus trap-policy parsing before normal operation.

Overlapping polarity claims fail validation while non-partitioning mask sets are healed by recomputation after logging, so silent correction can mask table-generation errors if diagnostics are ignored.
Unsorted register tables or entries exposing user state without reset handlers abort validation, risking boot failure if generated tables violate ordering or lifecycle contracts.

Translation setup must reject out-of-range bases and encodings as faults rather than walking them, and descriptor replacement must not proceed on unmapped or read-only slots; mishandling user-access faults or ignoring retry signals can corrupt guest tables or stall the emulator.

Granule translation maps architectural size selectors to page shifts twelve, fourteen and sixteen corresponding to four, sixteen and sixty-four kilobyte pages, with input address width defined as sixty-four minus the size field.
